sources.citation: Liu, Naijing & Dolma Choekyi Lama. 2026. [Kuke-English wordlist] dated 30 March 2026). 8 pp. ELAR collection SG1147 (dk0839), bundle ght0123 'Elicitation and orthography', hdl:2196/24o6nmn3-85ws-j9xs-9cli-d4bkjnfxa2b9.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose and no tone or stress marks; homophones are numbered (a1/a2, da1/da2/da3, changma1/changma2, dhue1/dhue2) rather than tone-marked.

sources.citation: Liu, Naijing & Dolma Choekyi Lama. 2026. Kuke Orthography (dated 30 March 2026). 2 pp. In: Documenting Kuke: the linguistic ecology of a 'stolen' language in Nepal, ELAR collection SG1147 (dk0839), bundle ght0123 'Elicitation and orthography', file, hdl:2196/71ghfn3r-8m29-kvrf-zz93-5744amv33haj.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No sentence on tone, pitch, stress or accent, and the orthography has no tone marks or tone letters. The only prosody-adjacent text is the (garbled in the original) note quoted below on non-modal/breathy voice and nasalisation. Long vowels are written with 'h' ('h is used for syllable with a single vowel or indicating long vowels, such as in Bihi'). The companion wordlist distinguishes homophonous spellings by indices (da1/da2/da3), which a human should check against the open ght0123/ght0124 recordings for a possible tonal contrast.

sources.citation: Liu, Naijing & Dolma Choekyi Lama. 2025-2026. Documenting Kuke: the linguistic ecology of a 'stolen' language in Nepal. ELAR collection dk0839 (ELDP small grant, University of Sydney; hdl:2196/3bd9079a-36c8-4c70-92e0-80b7efe66b55).
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: Collection landing page and ELDP project blurb read: audio-video corpus (conversations, elicitation, ELAN/Toolbox files); 'Language information' text covers speaker numbers, contact history and the 'stolen language' etymology only; nothing on phonology, tone or stress; no grammar/sketch listed yet.

sources.citation: Liu, Naijing. 2023. Segmental and prosodic phonology and morphophonology in Tsum, a language of Nepal. PhD thesis, Australian National University (hdl:1885/307369).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes TSUM (Tibetic neighbour), not Kuke. Kutang Ghale appears only in Table 1.2 (neighbouring Tamangic language) and p.13 (27% lexical similarity with Tsum per Webster 2022:10). No statement about Kuke phonology or stress. Saved because the author now holds the ELDP Kuke documentation grant.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages, Part 2, ch.10.7.3 (Tamangic contact languages).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only lists 'Kutang Ghale' among Tamangic languages (after Mazaudon 1978); nothing on its phonology.

sources.citation: Webster, Jeff. 2022 [orig. 1992]. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Tibeto-Burman Dialects of North Gorkha District, Nepal. Journal of Language Survey Reports. Dallas: SIL International. 120 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: The only published linguistic work with primary Kutang Ghale data (wordlists from Bihi and Chhak, transcription conventions); any remark on tone/stress in the wordlist phonology notes would be the sole first-hand statement. Normally open on sil.org but 403/offline by automated download during the run.

sources.citation: Gawne, Lauren & Kristine A. Hildebrandt. 2020. Reported speech in earthquake narratives from six Tibeto-Burman languages. Studies in Language 44(2): 461-499. doi:10.1075/sl.18028.gaw (green OA author version, La Trobe OPAL figshare 12611720).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Kutang tone or stress: a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for tone/tonal/stress/pitch/accent finds only generic remarks on prosodic cues to zero-marked quotation (section 6). p.6: 'a brief wordlist for Kutang (Webster 1992). This paper therefore represents some of the first analysis of these languages.'

sources.citation: Hildebrandt, Kristine, Tanner Burge-Beckley & Jacob Sebok. 2019. Language documentation in the aftermath of the 2015 Nepal earthquakes: A guide to two archives and a web exhibit. Language Documentation & Conservation 13: 618-651. hdl:10125/24914.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content. Extract of the Kutang passages. 10 MB PDF not.
